content: Discussion topic for #Project announcements > HuffmanCoding, Bzip2: Compression algorithms

Awesome to see more core compression algorithms implemented and verified in Lean! :tada:

When you get to the refinement-proof tier in TODO_BZIP2_COMPAT.md (bit reader/writer round-trip, canonical-Huffman round-trip, exact-block decoder/encoder refinement, malformed-input rejection completeness), you might find lean-zip's DEFLATE proofs useful for reference — different file format, but it's pretty similar requirements.

Most relevant files: Huffman.lean, HuffmanTheorems.lean, HuffmanKraft.lean, HuffmanCorrectLoop.lean for canonical Huffman; BitstreamWriteCorrect.lean, BitstreamCorrect.lean, BitstreamComplete.lean for bit I/O round-trip; InflateComplete.lean and DecodeComplete.lean for decoder-completeness against adversarial inputs. Just be aware these proofs are all AI-written, so treat with care. :-)

Have there been thoughts or plans of formalizing a notion of compression performance? I am not really deep into compression, but to my understanding the performance gets currently mostly measured by running it against some benchmarks and then seeing how fast / how much gets compressed.

Are there ways to formalize the notion of information theoretic compression in a somewhat universal way? Such as formalizing that a algorithm removes n-gram statistical structure from a bit string? Would love to hear your (probably more informed) thoughts on this.
